stories.body: Russian ballistic-missile strikes on Kyiv killed at least nine people and injured 28, including four children, Ukrainian officials said. Explosions were reported across the capital, where fires broke out, power outages hit some areas and residential buildings were damaged or partially collapsed, trapping residents. The attack came amid an escalation in Russian ballistic-missile attacks and as Ukraine faces shortages of Patriot interceptors, the only weapons in its arsenal capable of downing such missiles. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has sought US approval to produce Patriot missiles, but President Donald Trump said negotiations were continuing and Washington had not agreed to transfer the technology.
stories.headline: Russian ballistic-missile strikes on Kyiv kill at least nine people

stories.body: Hamas said it had agreed in principle to hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee under a US-backed roadmap for Gaza, but said disarmament depends on Israel ending its military campaign and withdrawing from the territory. The proposal calls for phased Hamas disarmament, a gradual Israeli withdrawal, Palestinian governance and an international stabilisation force. An Israeli official said Israeli troops would not withdraw from their current positions, including the so-called Yellow Line, until Hamas had undergone what Israel considers genuine disarmament. President Donald Trump said Israel was happy with the agreement, although Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called it unacceptable and other Israeli politicians voiced scepticism.
stories.headline: Hamas agrees in principle to disarm under a US-backed Gaza plan, while Israel sets conditions for withdrawal

stories.body: The World Meteorological Organization warned that a rapidly strengthening El Niño is likely to intensify heatwaves, droughts, floods and other extreme weather in coming months as it combines with human-caused global warming. Central Pacific sea-surface temperatures are projected to rise more than 2.9C above normal, with above-average temperatures expected across most land areas, especially Africa, southern Europe, South Asia, East Asia and South America. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said El Niño was “adding fuel to a planet already on fire” and urged governments to stop expanding coal, oil and gas projects. Scientists said the event could become exceptionally strong later this year, though projections remain uncertain.
stories.headline: UN warns a strengthening El Niño could intensify extreme heat on an already warming planet

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the second-largest ever recorded, with more than 3,500 confirmed infections and more than 1,500 deaths. The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, has spread through five eastern provinces since it was declared in May and is now the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic on record. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for the strain, while conflict, attacks on health facilities, aid cuts, mistrust of authorities and reliance on traditional healers have complicated containment efforts. Health officials and aid agencies warn that the true number of infections may be far higher than reported.
stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic becomes the world's second-largest outbreak

stories.body: The Trump administration is increasing the use of large immigration-court hearings and sharply shortening preparation time for migrants in an effort to reduce a longstanding case backlog, according to immigration-court data. More than 1,300 so-called mega master hearings were held in June, nearly three times the number held in the same month a year earlier, while many migrants are receiving little more than a month to prepare rather than about six months. Advocates say the pace is contributing to unprecedented numbers of missed hearings, deportation orders issued in absentia and asylum claims being deemed abandoned. Supporters of stricter immigration enforcement argue that faster proceedings are necessary to restore credibility to a system that often fails to reach final decisions.
stories.headline: A breakneck immigration-court pace is driving an increase in US deportation orders

stories.body: A Texas mother who was deported to Mexico despite holding valid DACA protection has sued the federal government after US Citizenship and Immigration Services said it intended to terminate her status for unauthorized travel on the day she was removed from the country. Jessica Treviño, 34, had DACA and a work permit valid until April 2027, but was arrested with her husband in December and deported in March. The Department of Homeland Security says she knowingly accepted voluntary departure and waived an appeal; Treviño says she signed no such forms and did not want to leave. Her lawsuit asks a federal court to rule that her removal was unlawful, require the government to facilitate her return and preserve her DACA protection.
stories.headline: US ends DACA status for a mother of three over alleged unauthorized travel

stories.body: US prosecutors have dropped charges against former Olympian David Hearn, who had faced up to 10 years in prison after being accused of damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. A court filing said newly obtained information strongly indicated that the damage was caused by a flawed, rushed installation carried out during renovations overseen by the Interior Department, rather than vandalism. President Donald Trump had publicly blamed vandals for damage to the pool, which was resealed and painted as part of a multimillion-dollar effort to beautify Washington before the US 250th Independence Day celebrations. Hearn's lawyers said the case should never have been brought and accused the administration of abusing government power.
stories.headline: US drops Reflecting Pool vandalism case, saying rushed renovations were botched

stories.body: At least 57 people died while trying to reach Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, after as many as 50,000 people crossed by land and sea over roughly 24 hours. The influx overwhelmed the city of about 85,000 residents and prompted Spain to deploy soldiers, police and Civil Guard officers. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez described the crossing as a violation of Spain's territorial integrity and blamed human-trafficking networks, while announcing a temporary reception centre and expedited procedures for people without a legal right to remain. Spain said more than 48,300 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco by Friday evening, while the EU prepared emergency discussions on the crisis.
stories.headline: At least 57 people die after tens of thousands cross from Morocco into Ceuta

stories.body: Spain's government has acknowledged that it did not anticipate the mass arrival of roughly 50,000 migrants into Ceuta, with a senior official saying the scale of the crossing could not have happened without an intelligence failure. Officials said attention had been focused on severe wildfires in central and western Spain, while early warnings from Ceuta's regional president and the Civil Guard about a rise in sea crossings were not treated as signs of an imminent crisis. Spain said more than 48,000 of those who entered the enclave had already returned voluntarily to Morocco. Migrants remaining in Ceuta described being motivated by reports on social media that crossing was easy and said they hoped to find work and a future in Europe.
stories.headline: Spain admits it did not foresee the Ceuta migration crisis as most arrivals return to Morocco

stories.body: Italy has announced temporary border controls for non-EU travellers arriving from Spain in response to the migration crisis in Ceuta, despite Spain saying that nearly all of the roughly 50,000 people who entered the enclave from Morocco had already returned. The measure will introduce checks at Italian ports and airports for non-European passengers travelling from Spain, while Spanish and other EU citizens will not face additional formalities. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called it an extraordinary national-security measure, and Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani cited concerns over uncontrolled migration and terrorism. France also said it would reinforce controls along its border with Spain, while Spain insisted that the integrity of the Schengen area remained fully guaranteed.
stories.headline: Italy imposes new border controls linked to the Ceuta crisis, raising tensions over Schengen

stories.body: A wildfire that has burned for nearly a week around La Vall d'Uixó in Valencia has been declared stabilised after scorching about 9,600 hectares, including a large area of the Sierra de Espadán natural park. Authorities lifted evacuation orders for residents of Artana and Eslida, the last communities still unable to return, but warned that the fire was not yet fully under control and could reignite. Firefighters will continue to cool hot spots and residents have been urged to stay away from the affected perimeter. Valencia's regional government announced a €67 million aid package for affected residents, municipalities, forest surveillance, prevention and reforestation, while extreme wildfire risk remains in place across the region.
stories.headline: Wildfire in Valencia's Sierra de Espadán is stabilized after burning nearly 9,600 hectares

stories.body: MTBVAC, a tuberculosis vaccine developed at Spain's University of Zaragoza and manufactured by Biofabri, is entering the decisive stage of clinical development and could be available from 2029 if trials succeed. It could become the first Spanish tuberculosis vaccine and only the second TB vaccine authorised globally since BCG entered use in 1921. A 5,500-participant trial in South Africa, Kenya and Tanzania is assessing whether the vaccine safely prevents pulmonary tuberculosis in adolescents and adults with latent infection. Supporters say ensuring affordable access in countries with the highest disease burden is central to the project, particularly because tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death among people living with HIV.
stories.headline: Spain's first tuberculosis vaccine, MTBVAC, moves closer to deployment

stories.body: A newly detected structural crack and small underground cavity near a Barcelona Metro Line 9 construction sinkhole have delayed the return of residents from four evacuated buildings in Sant Gervasi-la Bonanova until at least September. The sinkhole appeared on 7 July in the patio of a pizzeria near Putxet station, forcing the evacuation of eight buildings. Residents of three buildings have returned or are due to return shortly, but the buildings at Teodora Lamadrid 3 and 5 and Rubinstein 2 and 4 remain unsafe while ground-injection and stabilisation work continues. Authorities said financial advances for affected residents and businesses would begin to be processed, while the tunnel-boring machine remains halted.
stories.headline: A new cavity delays the return of residents displaced by Barcelona's L9 sinkhole

stories.body: Barcelona's ERC and Junts parties have demanded an urgent meeting of the TMB transport authority's board to explain the fire in the Line 1 overhead power system between Glòries and Clot stations and review how the emergency was handled. More than 100 passengers from an affected train were evacuated by walking along the tracks, and Junts said it was unacceptable that nearly 200 people had to flee through a smoke-filled tunnel without an orderly and safe evacuation. The parties want TMB to detail the cause of the incident, assess its safety procedures and outline changes to strengthen security on the metro network.
stories.headline: Barcelona parties demand explanations from TMB over the L1 metro fire and tunnel evacuation

stories.body: A judge has ordered the pretrial detention without bail of a man accused of killing his 34-year-old partner in Barcelona's Sant Martí district. The court also barred him from approaching or contacting the couple's two children and the victim's parents. Judicial documents say the woman was stabbed 11 times with a dagger, including wounds to her chest and head that caused fatal injuries to her lung and heart. The alleged attack occurred in front of the couple's children, aged eight and four, and two friends of the victim. The man fled after the killing but later turned himself in to the Mossos d'Esquadra police.
stories.headline: Man is remanded in custody over the killing of his partner in Barcelona's Sant Martí district
